canonical_digest.decimal_input_rule: no exponent and no leading zeros; trailing zeros are normalized away, never rejected
canonical_digest.field_order_rule: sorted keys; x-acp-order documents presentation order only and never changes digest bytes
canonical_digest.implementation_owner: B16 (src/acp_services/runtime/canonical_digest.py) - B03 freezes only the rules and vectors
canonical_digest.quantity_detection: exactly the keys {value, unit}; no other object is treated as a quantity
rules: the digest input is a JSON object; a non-object root is rejected (root_not_object)
drop_fields removes the listed top-level keys before canonicalization (proposal_digest uses this for volatile approval state)
object keys are sorted by Unicode code point; caller field order is irrelevant
keys MUST match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$ so code-point order is stable; a violation is rejected (non_canonical_key)

an object whose keys are exactly {value, unit} is a quantity: it is converted to the dimension base unit with Decimal(precision=28, ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and emitted as {unit, value} with a canonical decimal string
integers are JSON numbers; a quantity value is an integer or a plain-decimal string (no exponent, no leading zeros); trailing zeros are allowed on input and normalized away on output
JSON floats are a hard error anywhere (non_canonical_number); a digest input is never silently rounded
JSON null is forbidden anywhere in digest input (null_in_digest_input); omit the key instead
strings are normalized to Unicode NFC before serialization
serialization is UTF-8 without BOM, no insignificant whitespace (separators ',' and ':'), no trailing newline, ensure_ascii=False
arrays are order-significant unless the parent key is listed in set_fields, in which case elements are sorted by their canonical JSON string (UTF-8 byte order)
digest = 'sha256:' + lowercase hex of sha256(canonical UTF-8 bytes)
canonical_digest.signature: canonical_digest(value: dict, *, set_fields: tuple[str, ...] = (), drop_fields: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> str

state_model.source: src/acp_services/store/records.py::JobStatus (no new status is introduced by this contract)

dispositions.job_spec: Mapped onto the effective JobSpec field named by the policy row by every entry.
dispositions.legacy_allowlist: Accepted for a named consumer set, never used for execution, with a removal version and exit condition. Empty in v1 (M0-06 inventory found no undeclared field in use); there is deliberately no 'ignore unknown fields and warn' mode.
dispositions.request_control: schema_version / idempotency_key / preflight_fingerprint; never part of the scientific plan.
dispositions.server_path_rejected: A client may not choose a server filesystem path. Declared so the rejection is explicit (params.rule=unsupported_server_path), rejected at http and mcp.

config_path.reason: The Controller owns its configuration sources; a client-chosen host path is refused with params.rule=unsupported_server_path.

extensions.note: Namespaced extension metadata (unknown_field_policy U4); opaque to the platform and never used for execution.

idempotency_key.note: Raw client retry key; excluded from the request digest.

output_dir.reason: The Controller allocates the task directory; a client-chosen path is refused with params.rule=unsupported_server_path.

submit_field_policy.freeze: v1 extra=forbid: an undeclared execution field is never forwarded to a task. HTTP answers 422 input_invalid with params.rule=unknown_field; MCP answers the same code/params locally; the CLI emits one structured error object.
submit_field_policy.preflight_field_set: same as submit (preflight is the dry run of the same normalized request); naming/tags/research fields never enter the plan digest

request_digest.compatibility: A pre-M0-06 row (version 1) replays when its stored digest equals the current digest or re-derives from the v1 field table.
request_digest.rule: The row persists (request_digest_version, digest) and the full effective request. Equal digest bytes always mean the same request; a row of another version is verified against its own frozen field table. An unverifiable row is a reconcile conflict — never 'tampered' and never a silent second task.

submit_key_policy.cli: same as HTTP: the operator-supplied key is forwarded; omitting it is non-idempotent
submit_key_policy.cross_tenant_rule: two tenants reusing one short key is a typed conflict (revision_conflict, params.rule=idempotency_scope_conflict), never a replay
submit_key_policy.http: optional on the manual/legacy path; a key-less HTTP submit is an explicitly NON-IDEMPOTENT call (a retry may create a second task) and never reports idempotent_replay=true
submit_key_policy.mcp: REQUIRED: a key-less acp_submit is input_invalid with params.rule=idempotency_key_required and creates nothing (M1-01b)
submit_key_policy.migration_note: 1.3.0 clients that sent no key now receive input_invalid/idempotency_key_required instead of a created task; mint a UUID or '<client>:<project>:<round>:<call>' before the first submit. Unknown execution fields were already rejected (rule=unknown_field) and remain so.
submit_key_policy.namespace_rule: the raw key is a global namespace per action (across projects/principals/entries); use a high-entropy UUID or a namespaced key embedding project/research/round

nullable_policy.digest_input: null is forbidden in digest input; omit the key instead
nullable_policy.forbidden: dropping a key to mean null on a response; responses MUST emit the key with null

numeric_bound_policy.exclusive_bounds: unsupported; a producer needing an open bound expresses it as an inclusive bound plus a decimal step documented in description
numeric_bound_policy.numbers: integers only as JSON numbers; non-integer quantities are canonical decimal strings (see canonical_digest)

one_of_policy.requirement: branches MUST be mutually exclusive and carry exactly one x-acp-discriminator property name that is also a required const/enum property in every branch

ui_schema_subset.purpose: The keyword subset a client (C Workbench form renderer, RPH Bridge) MUST support and the producer (A descriptor, B discovery) MUST stay inside. This is not a full JSON Schema 2020-12 renderer; constraints outside the subset are a producer defect and MUST be rejected by the consumer, never silently ignored.

ref_policy.allowed: local JSON Pointer inside the same document: "#/$defs/<name>"
ref_policy.decision_owner: A produces the descriptor; B discovery forwards it without rewriting scientific fields; C renders only this subset
ref_policy.pre_expansion: producers MAY pre-expand $ref; pre-expanded and $ref forms MUST describe the same instance set
ref_policy.remote_refs: remote refs are unsupported: a consumer MUST reject a descriptor with a non-local $ref and report error_class invalid-parameter

ui_schema_subset.unknown_keyword_policy: an instance keyword not in supported_keywords and not namespaced x-acp-* is a producer defect: consumer rejects with invalid-parameter

unknown_field_policy.execution_field_allowlist_note: input, method and resources are A-owned payload mappings (see science-binding.v1.json). Unknown keys INSIDE input/method are governed by A's TaskRequest rule S2 (unknown fields ignored on parse); the platform does not interpret them. The envelope-level rejection in U1 prevents an unknown envelope field from ever reaching an executor.

rules.rule: A new execution request rejects any field not declared in this contract (additional_properties=false). Unknown execution fields are never forwarded to a task.

rules.eligibility_effect: none - a preserved unknown field grants no execution, recovery or approval eligibility
rules.rule: A read of historical facts preserves unknown fields verbatim (round-trip), so an older client never destroys newer data.
schema_version is a major version. Any value other than 1 is an unknown major version: the request MUST NOT create or mutate a task; execution is refused.
Extra metadata lives ONLY under the top-level extensions object, keyed by a namespaced identifier; extension values are opaque to the platform and never influence execution.
